goal:
Answer the question using only the papers in this directory.

What ImageNet top-5 error does the original ResNet paper report for its ILSVRC'15 ensemble, and what single-crop and 10-crop top-5 errors does DenseNet report for DenseNet-201? Identify the data split and model/evaluation setup for each. Can these numbers establish a like-for-like head-to-head advantage?

Papers:
- 1512.03385v1.pdf
- 1608.06993v5.pdf

No: these are not like-for-like (ensemble vs single model; test vs validation; crop protocol not matched), so they cannot establish a head-to-head advantage.", "explanation": "In 1512.03385v1.pdf, the ILSVRC’15 entry is an ensemble: the authors combine six models of different depth (only two 152-layer ones at submission) and report 3.57% top-5 error on the test set, winning ILSVRC 2015 [S:154860ab87fe#62]. Table 5 likewise labels the 3.57% ResNet result as an ensemble error on the ImageNet test set reported by the test server [S:154860ab87fe#53]. In 1608.06993v5.pdf, Table 3 reports DenseNet-201 at 22.58/21.46 top-1 and 6.34/5.54 top-5 for single-crop/10-crop testing, explicitly on the ImageNet validation set [S:63d1b0f26659#48]. The DenseNet ImageNet setup uses ILSVRC 2012 (1.2M training, 50k validation, 1,000 classes), 224x224 single- or 10-crop testing, and reports validation errors [S:63d1b0f26659#46]. citations.title: arXiv:1512.03385v1  [cs.CV]  10 Dec 2015
citations.text:
Comparisons with State-of-the-art Methods. In Table 4
we compare with the previous best single-model results.
Our baseline 34-layer ResNets have achieved very compet-
itive accuracy. Our 152-layer ResNet has a single-model
top-5 validation error of 4.49%. This single-model result
outperforms all previous ensemble results (Table 5). We
combine six models of different depth to form an ensemble
(only with two 152-layer ones at the time of submitting).
This leads to 3.57% top-5 error on the test set (Table 5).
This entry won the 1st place in ILSVRC 2015.

citations.title: arXiv:1608.06993v5  [cs.CV]  28 Jan 2018
citations.text:
We simply replace the ResNet model with the DenseNet-
BC network, and keep all the experiment settings exactly
the same as those used for ResNet.
We report the single-crop and 10-crop validation errors
of DenseNets on ImageNet in Table 3.
Figure 3 shows
the single-crop top-1 validation errors of DenseNets and
ResNets as a function of the number of parameters (left) and
FLOPs (right). The results presented in the ﬁgure reveal that
DenseNets perform on par with the state-of-the-art ResNets,
whilst requiring signiﬁcantly fewer parameters and compu-
tation to achieve comparable performance. For example, a
DenseNet-201 with 20M parameters model yields similar
validation error as a 101-layer ResNet with more than 40M
parameters. Similar trends can be observed from the right
panel, which plots the validation error as a function of the
number of FLOPs: a DenseNet that requires as much com-
putat

citations.title: arXiv:1608.06993v5  [cs.CV]  28 Jan 2018
citations.text:
ion as a ResNet-50 performs on par with a ResNet-101,
which requires twice as much computation.
It is worth noting that our experimental setup implies
that we use hyperparameter settings that are optimized for
ResNets but not for DenseNets. It is conceivable that more
extensive hyper-parameter searches may further improve
the performance of DenseNet on ImageNet.

stop: The evidence already covers all sub-questions: ResNet reports 3.57% top-5 for its ILSVRC'15 ensemble on the ImageNet test set; DenseNet-201 reports 6.34% single-crop and 5.54% 10-crop top-5 on the ImageNet validation set.
